arguments.summary: Investigation into a suspected APT-29 intrusion revealed a compromised low-criticality IT workstation (WS-IT-101) originating from external IP 203.0.113.88. Initial scan activity was detected and blocked. The user on the affected system (CORP\helpdesk) exhibited normal behavior patterns. No direct evidence of compromise was found on engineering hosts (WS-ENG-015, WS-ENG-022, SRV-BUILD-01) despite initial alerts. Further investigation was restricted due to tool access limitations in the Analyze and Admin phases.

timeline.description: External IP 203.0.113.88 detected conducting a SYN scan against WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Activity blocked by IDS.
Successful authentication to WS-IT-101 by user CORP\helpdesk from internal network.
Initial triage of WS-ENG-015 shows normal process tree and network connections (chrome.exe to Google). UEBA score for user jdoe is low (0.35).
SIEM search confirms scan activity from 203.0.113.88 and subsequent internal login. Access to EDR/NDR and IDS/CMDB tools denied in Analyze phase, halting deeper investigation.
All remediation tools (EDR, IAM, Firewall, Config) denied in Admin phase. Incident response effectively blocked.

        src_ip|cidr: 10.0.0.0/8|not
        protocol: tcp
        flags: S
        count(dst_port) > 100
    timeframe: 60s
    condition: selection
level: high

arguments.summary: Credential compromise on workstation WS-FIN-AP01 initiated via phishing email with malicious macro. Adversary executed encoded PowerShell from Outlook, loaded unsigned beacon DLL via rundll32, and established C2 communication. Source IP 185.220.101.42 blocked, user jsmith credentials reset, and host hardened via Ansible.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted Nmap SYN scan against internal IT asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15).
User CORP\jsmith opened Outlook, initiating the attack chain.
Malicious macro executed, spawning hidden encoded PowerShell process (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011).
Established persistent C2 beacon over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Incident detected and response initiated.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 185.220.101.42.
User CORP\jsmith credentials reset and MFA re-enrollment initiated.
Full endpoint scan completed; PUP detected but unrelated to breach.
Hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-AP01 to reduce attack surface.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Spawned from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
condition:
  - CommandLine|contains: 'powershell'
  - ParentProcessName|endswith: 'outlook.exe'
  - CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  - ProcessIntegrityLevel: 'Medium'
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule Suspicious_Rundll32_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from user Temp directories"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE T1218.011"
        maltype = "backdoor"
    strings:
        $s1 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" nocase
        $s2 = "rundll32.exe" nocase
        $s3 = ".dll" nocase
    condition:
        $s2 and $s1 and $s3
}
